newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner - EMU delay to have limited impact on mark.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner - EMU delay to have limited impact on mark.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG management board member Gerd Haeusler said on Monday a delay of European monetary union would result in a far smaller appreciation in the mark than generally thought.

"I would personally consider a short-term reaction by the financial markets as conceivable, but to a far smaller extent than is mostly thought," said Hauesler, a top executive at Dresdner, which is Germany's second-biggest bank.

Haeusler, a former Bundesbank directorate member who joined Dresdner last year, said current exchange rates in Europe and beyond at the moment better reflected economic fundamentals than had been the case in recent years.
"There is virtually no currency whose current exchange rate to the mark would not be justifiable," Haeusler said.
Hauesler also said debt markets in France, Italy and Spain were far less susceptible to speculative attacks than was the case in 1992.
Also, if the mark did appreciate in response to a delay, it was very likely that the European Union central banks would respond to the appreciation by changing interest rates.

"It must not be overlooked that in the Bundesbank's arsenal of arguments, the exchange rate has a much greater significance than it used to. In the unlikely case of a steep mark appreciation, I regard it as very likely that the Bundesbank would intervene with a vigorous interest rate cut, possibly even beforehand," said Haeusler.
The final factor against the mark strengthening is that the mark would be unlikely to appreciate if Germany had been unable to meet the fiscal criteria for EMU.
